final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. Final summary:

**Case N42 — peripheral nerve sheath tumor (T2 MRI)**

- **Finding:** a large (~44 × 27 × 27 mm) T2-hyperintense, lobulated, encapsulated mass in the left posterior thigh, with a bright heterogeneous core and a thinner bright periphery that tapers superiorly and into a thin inferior tail.
- **Workflow:** located on axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets → seeded with two positive points on the brightest core (v1, 12.9 mL) → tested an intensity candidate (C2) that leaked into the medial dark fascial plane and reverted it → re-ran a lasso around the whole lesion to tighten the boundary (v3, 11.5 mL) → `seg_refine` for boundary smoothing (v4, 11.4 mL, only −0.1 mL change, confirming stability).
- **Validation:** zoomed checks in all three planes showed the outline hugging the bright tumor margin; end-slices 8 mm past both poles contained no lesion tissue; no stray components. The external bright medial band and the long vertical bright streaks were identified as vessels/fascia and deliberately excluded.
- **Final mask:** single component, 11.4 mL, extent axial 25–66, coronal 35–61, sagittal 24–49. Saved with **medium** confidence (minor uncertainty about the very thin peripheral capsule, omitted to avoid leakage).
